visual_goal: Show every finance process converging on Record-to-Report, with treasury and tax as shared services the operational processes call, and the results flowing right to planning and disclosure.
prompt: A left-to-right convergence illustration. At the far left, five boxes stacked vertically: 'Procure-to-Pay', 'Order-to-Cash', 'Partner payouts', 'Acquire-to-Retire', 'Hire-to-Retire'. In the centre, a large round hub labeled 'Record-to-Report', drawn as an open book inside a circle. One thick arrow from each of the five left boxes into the hub (five arrows). Above the hub, a service desk labeled 'Treasury'; below the hub, a service desk labeled 'Tax'. Each desk has one thick arrow down or up into the hub (two arrows). Thin dotted arrows show calls into the desks: from 'Procure-to-Pay' and 'Partner payouts' to 'Treasury', and from 'Procure-to-Pay' and 'Order-to-Cash' to 'Tax'. At the right of the hub, one arrow to a box 'Plan-to-Perform' and one arrow to a document stack 'Filing and disclosure'.
alt: Procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, partner payouts, acquire-to-retire and hire-to-retire all flow into a central record-to-report hub; treasury and tax are shared desks the processes call, which also post into the hub; the hub feeds plan-to-perform and filing and disclosure.

visual_goal: Show Procure-to-Pay crossing four systems and a bank, with each hand-off between systems marked as needing an identifier, a control total and an exception owner.
prompt: A left-to-right flow across four tall panels side by side, each a different soft colour, labeled at the top: 'Procurement', 'ERP', 'Treasury', 'Bank'. Inside each panel sits one icon: a shopping basket with a box in 'Procurement', a server with an open book in 'ERP', a vault in 'Treasury', a plain columned bank building with a smooth blank triangular roof in 'Bank'. Near the top of the 'ERP' panel, just under its title and above the server, sits a smaller lilac box 'Tax engine', connected down to the ERP server by one short vertical double-headed arrow labeled 'Tax lines'. Upper row of arrows, all pointing right: from the basket to the ERP server labeled 'Invoice'; from the ERP server to the vault labeled 'Payment file'; from the vault to the bank building labeled 'Payment'. Lower row, near the bottom of the picture, one long return arrow starts under the bank building, runs left through 'Treasury', and turns up to end at the underside of the ERP server, labeled 'Statement'. On every arrow, exactly where it crosses a panel border, sits one small round badge holding three tiny icons side by side: a barcode tag, a sigma sum sign and a person silhouette.
alt: Procure-to-pay crosses procurement, the ERP, a tax engine, treasury and the bank; every crossing — invoice, tax lines, payment file, payment and returning statements — carries a hand-off badge for identifier, control total and exception owner.

visual_goal: Show Book-to-Settle as swimlanes: booking, money and accounting run in different systems on different clocks, and the three-way match is where they are proven to agree.
prompt: A swimlane illustration with four horizontal lanes stacked top to bottom, each with a different small clock icon at its left end showing a different time, and a lane label: 'Booking', 'Payments', 'Finance platform', 'Payouts'. In 'Booking': two boxes 'Booking confirmed' and further right 'Stay completed'. In 'Payments': two boxes 'Capture' and far to the right 'Settlement'. In 'Finance platform': two boxes 'Liability' and further right 'Revenue'. In 'Payouts': one box 'Bank confirmation' near the right. Exactly four lightning-bolt event arrows, each pointing down: from 'Booking confirmed' to 'Liability', from 'Capture' to 'Liability', from 'Stay completed' to 'Revenue', and from 'Revenue' to 'Bank confirmation'. 'Settlement' sits to the right of the 'Stay completed' column so that its only arrow goes right, into the scale. At the far right, spanning the lower three lanes, a large balance scale with three pans labeled 'Three-way match'. Exactly three arrows enter the scale: one from 'Settlement', one from 'Revenue', one from 'Bank confirmation'.
alt: Four swimlanes — booking, payments, finance platform and payouts — each on its own clock; booking and capture events create the liability, stay completion triggers revenue and the payout, and settlement, revenue and bank confirmations all meet at a three-way match on the right.
